thread:
Alejandra: @here Quick heads-up — we're starting a staged rollout of the new Prompt Instrumentation & Telemetry policy and corresponding SDK surface for capturing non-sensitive prompt metadata. Goal: better production debugging and quality telemetry without collecting raw user content by default.

Elaine: TL;DR: SDKs will add an optional prompt_metadata field (dictionary) and a runtime flag to enable limited prompt logging. Default is OFF for hosted and private installs.

Devon: Timeline: docs + migration guide live next week, py/js minor releases with the new param will ship in 7 days, opt-in period for customers = 30 days, after which the metadata field will be available for Redwood internal telemetry only when customers explicitly opt in.

Sven: Privacy notes — important: we will not store raw prompt text for telemetry by default. What we capture when enabled: template_id, source, fingerprint (SHA256 of prompt with salt), language tag, and safe flags. No PII, no raw tokens unless customer uses the explicit 'allow_raw_prompt_logging' opt-in and signs the Data Processing Addendum (DPA). For Private deployments customers can control retention via KMS/DB settings.

Elaine: Example SDK usage (py):
```python
resp = client.generate(
  prompt,
  prompt_metadata={"template_id": "home-search-v2", "source": "ui-search"}
)
```
Env toggle (all runtimes):
```bash
REDWOOD_PROMPT_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false # default
REDWOOD_PROMPT_TELEMETRY_ALLOW_RAW=false  # must be explicit true to send raw text
```
PR for the py/js changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4912 (WIP).

Devon: Docs changes include a migration guide, a short FAQ about privacy/compliance, a quick audit checklist for SSO & KMS, and a sample dev workflow for enabling telemetry only in staging.

Alejandra: Docs note will include copy for customer support and a sample email template for notifying customers about the optional telemetry feature. I'll post the draft in #docs for review later today.

Sven: Compliance folks — if you want to run through the DPA language before we flip anything to required-for-internal-telemetry, ping me. This should be fine for SOC/PEN audits as long as retention and hashing are documented.

Elaine: Small implementation detail — for low-latency paths we batch-send hashed fingerprints only; we won't attach metadata that increases per-request token costs. The SDK will expose a lightweight builder: `PromptMetadataBuilder.from_template(id, attrs...)`

Devon: Rollout plan (short):
- Week 0: Announce + docs draft (this thread).
- Week 1: SDK minor releases + migration examples, opt-in telemetry flag available.
- Weeks 2-4: Customer opt-in period, collect feedback.
- Week 5+: Policy enforced for Redwood internal telemetry only for opted-in customers or when customers have accepted DPA changes.

Alejandra: FAQs to prep: how to opt out, where telemetry is stored, who can access it. I'll add those.

Elaine: If you want to try it locally: clone and run `pip install -e .` on the branch, config via env vars above. I can drop a quick demo snippet in #dev-examples tomorrow.

Sven: Quick clarifier for partners & private installs: we will not push opt-in defaults to customers; Private deployments get the same default OFF behavior and control via the admin console.

Devon: Thanks all — please react with :thumbsup: if you're good, or drop questions here.
